stem: In the primary survey of this trauma patient, which grouping of signs and observations would best indicate adequate breathing?

options.text: Respiratory Rate, Chest wall expansion, Subcostal/Intercostal Recession, Tracheal Tug
Oxygen Saturations and Skin Colour, Heart Rate, and Conscious level
Air entry (Equal bilateral) and Added sounds

explanation: Option C best assesses breathing adequacy by checking air entry and the presence of added breath sounds, which can indicate pneumothorax, haemothorax, or other thoracic injury. The other options include signs relevant to broader physiological status or work of breathing, but C most directly evaluates the effectiveness of ventilation on auscultation.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: In trauma primary survey, breathing assessment includes inspection, chest movement, work of breathing, and auscultation for air entry and added sounds. This option best matches that focus.

optionExplanations.A: These are useful observations of respiratory effort, but they do not directly assess whether air is moving into both lungs or whether there are abnormal breath sounds.
optionExplanations.B: These are important overall observations, but they are not the best grouping to indicate efficacy of breathing in the primary survey.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Equal bilateral air entry and absence/presence of added sounds directly assess ventilation and help identify chest injury.

Clinical scenario 1 - James

Teaching/learning points:

Initial ABC approach to trauma patient

Recognition of life-threatening injury and resuscitation priorities

You receive a pre-hospital alert from paramedics regarding James, a four year-old boy who ran away from his mother onto the road, where he was hit by a van at approximately 50kph. He hit the windscreen and was thrown approximately 7 metres. He was unconscious at the scene and not moving spontaneously. The paramedic crew on the scene report him to be unconscious but breathing, with a respiratory rate of 30/min, heart rate 120bpm, multiple abrasions and bruises. ETA 10 minutes.

The following 12 questions refer to James' clinical scenario.
